rationale: A wins because it knows where the facts stop and says so out loud: "Every claim about bank revenue impact is currently an inference, not a fact you gave me" is exactly the discipline this assignment needs. B has usable shapes, but it keeps writing checks the update cannot cash, especially "FedNow just got its most significant commercial test" and "Plaid spent a decade building the data pipes." That is not strategy; that is a reporter finding the weak floorboard before you do.
gaps_in_A: "FedNow adoption stories have mostly been about disbursements and B2B" adds unsourced market context not supplied in the update.
"The 70% saving only shows up on big-ticket sales" slightly overstates the given fact; Plaid said "up to 70% lower" on large transactions, not that savings only exist there.
"Plaid needs 12,000 banks to help route payments past the fees banks collect" is a sharp tension, but bank revenue impact is still an inference and should stay framed as a question.
gaps_in_B: "FedNow just got its most significant commercial test" is an unsupported superlative. No evidence says this is FedNow's biggest commercial test.
"Plaid spent a decade building the data pipes" invents company-history framing not in the update.
"competing simultaneously with Stripe and Adyen" is not supplied. That may be true market context, but this prompt did not give it to you.
"The network density is what makes this different from prior A2A attempts" invents a comparative claim without proof.
